{{short description|Associative algebra introduced by Richard Brauer}}
In mathematics, a '''Brauer algebra''' is an [[associative algebra]] introduced by [[Richard Brauer]]<ref name="bra37"/> in the context of the [[representation theory]] of the [[orthogonal group]]. It plays the same role that the [[symmetric group]] does for the representation theory of the [[general linear group]] in [[Schur–Weyl duality]].

== Structure ==

The Brauer algebra <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> is a <math>\mathbb{Z}[\delta]</math>-algebra depending on the choice of a positive integer <math>n</math>. Here <math>\delta</math> is an indeterminate, but in practice <math>\delta</math> is often specialised to the dimension of the [[fundamental representation]] of an [[orthogonal group]] <math>O(\delta)</math>. The Brauer algebra has the dimension

:<math>\dim\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta) = \frac{(2n)!}{2^n n!} = (2n-1)!! = (2n-1)(2n-3)\cdots 5\cdot 3\cdot 1</math>

=== Diagrammatic definition ===

[[Image:Brauer algebra.jpg|thumb|400px|The product of 2 basis elements ''A'' and ''B'' of the Brauer algebra with ''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;12]]

A basis of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> consists of all pairings on a set of <math>2n</math> elements <math>X_1, ..., X_n, Y_1, ..., Y_n</math> (that is, all [[perfect matching]]s of a [[complete graph]] <math>K_{2n}</math>: any two of the <math>2n</math> elements may be matched to each other, regardless of their symbols). The elements <math>X_i</math> are usually written in a row, with the elements <math>Y_i</math> beneath them.

The product of two basis elements <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> is obtained by concatenation: first identifying the endpoints in the bottom row of  <math>A</math> and the top row of <math>B</math> (Figure ''AB '' in the diagram), then deleting the endpoints in the middle row and joining endpoints in the remaining two rows if they are joined, directly or by a path, in ''AB '' (Figure  ''AB=nn'' in the diagram). Thereby all closed loops in the middle of ''AB'' are removed. The product <math>A\cdot B</math> of the basis elements is then defined to be the basis element corresponding to the new pairing multiplied by <math>\delta^r</math> where <math>r</math> is the number of deleted loops. In the example <math>A\cdot B = \delta^{2} AB</math>.

=== Generators and relations ===

<math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> can also be defined as the <math>\mathbb{Z}[\delta]</math>-algebra with generators <math>s_1,\ldots,s_{n-1}, e_1, \ldots, e_{n-1}</math> satisfying the following relations:

* Relations of the [[symmetric group]]:
:<math>s_i^2 = 1</math>
:<math>s_i s_j = s_j s_i</math> whenever <math>|i-j|>1</math>
:<math>s_i s_{i+1} s_i = s_{i+1} s_i s_{i+1}</math>
* Almost-[[idempotent]] relation:
:<math>e_i^2 = \delta e_i</math>
* Commutation:
:<math>e_i e_j = e_j e_i</math>
:<math>s_i e_j = e_j s_i</math>
:whenever<math>|i-j|>1</math>
* Tangle relations
:<math>e_i e_{i\pm 1} e_i = e_i</math>
:<math>s_i s_{i\pm 1} e_i = e_{i\pm 1} e_i</math>
:<math>e_i s_{i\pm 1} s_i = e_i e_{i\pm 1}</math>
* Untwisting:
:<math>s_i e_i = e_i s_i = e_i</math>:
:<math>e_i s_{i\pm 1} e_i = e_i</math>

In this presentation <math>s_i</math> represents the diagram in which <math>X_k</math> is always connected to <math>Y_k</math> directly beneath it except for <math>X_i</math> and <math>X_{i+1}</math> which are connected to <math>Y_{i+1}</math> and <math>Y_i</math> respectively. Similarly <math>e_i</math> represents the diagram in which <math>X_k</math> is always connected to <math>Y_k</math> directly beneath it except for <math>X_i</math> being connected to <math>X_{i+1}</math> and <math>Y_i</math> to <math>Y_{i+1}</math>.

=== Basic properties ===

The Brauer algebra is a [[subalgebra]] of the [[partition algebra]].

The Brauer algebra <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> is [[semisimple algebra|semisimple]] if <math>\delta\in\mathbb{C}-\{0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\dots,\pm n\}</math>.<ref name="bm05"/><ref name="wen88"/>

The subalgebra of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> generated by the generators <math>s_i</math> is the [[group ring|group algebra]] of the symmetric group <math>S_n</math>.

The subalgebra of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> generated by the generators <math>e_i</math> is the [[Temperley-Lieb algebra]] <math>TL_n(\delta)</math>.<ref name="hj18"/>

The Brauer algebra is a [[cellular algebra]].

For a pairing <math>A</math> let <math>n(A)</math> be the number of closed loops formed by identifying <math>X_i</math> with <math>Y_i</math> for any <math>i=1,2,\dots,n</math>: then the '''Jones trace''' <math>\text{Tr}(A) = \delta^{n(A)}</math> obeys <math>\text{Tr}(AB)=\text{Tr}(BA)</math> i.e. it is indeed a [[Trace (linear algebra)#Generalizations|trace]].

== Representations ==

=== Brauer-Specht modules ===

Brauer-Specht modules are finite-dimensional modules of the Brauer algebra. 
If <math>\delta</math> is such that <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> is semisimple,
they form a complete set of simple modules of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math>.<ref name="hj18"/> These modules are parametrized by [[partition (number theory)|partitions]], because they are built from the [[Specht modules]] of the [[symmetric group]], which are themselves parametrized by partitions.

For <math>0\leq \ell \leq n</math> with <math>\ell\equiv n\bmod 2</math>, let <math>B_{n,\ell}</math> be the set of perfect matchings of <math>n+\ell</math> elements <math>X_1,\dots ,X_n,Y_1,\dots ,Y_\ell</math>, such that <math>Y_j</math> is matched with one of the <math>n</math> elements <math>X_1,\dots ,X_n</math>. For any ring <math>k</math>, the space <math>kB_{n,\ell}</math> is a left <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math>-module, where basis elements of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> act by graph concatenation. (This action can produce matchings that violate the restriction that <math>Y_1,\dots ,Y_\ell</math> cannot match with one another: such graphs must be modded out.) Moreover, the space <math>kB_{n,\ell}</math> is a right <math>S_\ell</math>-module.<ref name="mar09"/>

Given a [[Specht module]] <math>V_\lambda</math> of <math>kS_\ell</math>, where <math>\lambda</math> is a partition of <math>\ell</math> (i.e. <math>|\lambda|=\ell</math>), the corresponding '''Brauer-Specht module''' of <math>\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> is 
:<math>
W_{\lambda} = kB_{n,|\lambda|} \otimes_{kS_{|\lambda|}} V_\lambda \qquad \big(|\lambda|\leq n, |\lambda|\equiv n\bmod 2\big)
</math>
A basis of this module is the set of elements <math>b\otimes v</math>, where <math>b\in B_{n,|\lambda|}</math> is such that the <math>|\lambda|</math> lines that end on elements <math>Y_j</math> do not cross, and <math>v</math> belongs to a basis of <math>V_\lambda</math>.<ref name="mar09"/> The dimension is 
:<math>
\dim(W_\lambda) = \binom{n}{|\lambda|} (n-|\lambda|-1)!! \dim(V_\lambda)
</math>
i.e. the product of a [[binomial coefficient]], a [[double factorial]], and the dimension of the corresponding Specht module, which is given by the [[hook length formula]].

=== Schur-Weyl duality ===

Let <math>V=\mathbb{R}^d</math> be a Euclidean [[vector space]] of dimension <math>d</math>, and <math>O(V)=O(d,\mathbb{R})</math> the corresponding orthogonal group. Then write <math>B_n(d)</math> for the specialisation <math>\mathbb{R}\otimes_{\mathbb{Z}[\delta]}\mathfrak{B}_n(\delta)</math> where <math>\delta</math> acts on <math>\mathbb{R}</math> by multiplication with <math>d</math>. The [[tensor product|tensor power]] <math>V^{\otimes n} := \underbrace{V\otimes\cdots\otimes V}_{n\text{ times}}</math> is naturally a <math>B_n(d)</math>-[[module (mathematics)|module]]: <math>s_i</math> acts by switching the <math>i</math>th and <math>(i+1)</math>th tensor factor and <math>e_i</math> acts by contraction followed by expansion in the <math>i</math>th and <math>(i+1)</math>th tensor factor, i.e. <math>e_i</math> acts as

:<math>v_1\otimes \cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes\Big(v_i\otimes v_{i+1}\Big)\otimes\cdots \otimes v_n \mapsto v_1\otimes \cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes\left(\langle v_i, v_{i+1}\rangle \sum_{k=1}^d (w_k\otimes w_k)\right)\otimes\cdots \otimes v_n</math>

where <math>w_1,\ldots,w_d</math> is any [[orthonormal basis]] of <math>V</math>. (The sum is in fact independent of the choice of this basis.)

This action is useful in a generalisation of the [[Schur-Weyl duality]]: if <math>d\geq n</math>, the image of <math>B_n(d)</math> inside <math>\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes n})</math> is the centraliser of <math>O(V)</math> inside <math>\operatorname{End}(V^{\otimes n})</math>, and conversely the image of <math>O(V)</math> is the centraliser of <math>B_n(d)</math>.<ref name="bm05"/> The tensor power <math>V^{\otimes n}</math> is therefore both an <math>O(V)</math>- and a <math>B_n(d)</math>-module and satisfies
:<math>V^{\otimes n} = \bigoplus_{\lambda} U_\lambda \boxtimes W_\lambda</math>
where <math>\lambda</math> runs over a subset of the [[Partition (number theory)|partitions]] such that <math>|\lambda|\leq n</math> and <math>|\lambda|\equiv n \bmod 2</math>,
<math>U_\lambda</math> is an irreducible <math>O(V)</math>-module, and <math>W_\lambda</math> is a Brauer-Specht module of 
<math>B_n(d)</math>.

It follows that the Brauer algebra has a natural action on the space of polynomials on <math>V^n</math>, which commutes with the action of the orthogonal group.

If <math>\delta</math> is a negative even [[integer]], the Brauer algebra is related by Schur-Weyl duality to the [[symplectic group]] <math>\text{Sp}_{-\delta}(\mathbb{C})</math>, rather than the orthogonal group.

==Walled Brauer algebra==

The walled Brauer algebra <math>\mathfrak{B}_{r,s}(\delta)</math> is a subalgebra of <math>\mathfrak{B}_{r+s}(\delta)</math>. Diagrammatically, it consists of diagrams where the only allowed pairings are of the types <math>X_{i\leq r}-X_{j>r}</math>, <math>Y_{i\leq r}-Y_{j>r}</math>, <math>X_{i\leq r}-Y_{j\leq r}</math>, <math>X_{i>r} - Y_{j>r}</math>. This amounts to having a wall that separates <math>X_{i\leq r},Y_{i\leq r}</math> from <math>X_{i>r},Y_{i>r}</math>, and requiring that <math>X-Y</math> pairings cross the wall while <math>X-X,Y-Y</math> pairings don't.<ref name="cvdm07"/>

The walled Brauer algebra is generated by <math>\{s_i\}_{1\leq i\leq r+s-1,i\neq r} \cup\{e_r\}</math>. These generators obey the basic relations of <math>\mathfrak{B}_{r+s}(\delta)</math> that involve them, plus the two relations<ref name="bo19"/>
:<math> 
e_rs_{r+1}s_{r-1}e_r s_{r-1} = e_rs_{r+1}s_{r-1}e_r s_{r+1} \quad , \quad s_{r-1}e_rs_{r+1}s_{r-1}e_r  = s_{r+1}e_rs_{r+1}s_{r-1}e_r 
</math>
(In <math>\mathfrak{B}_{r+s}(\delta)</math>, these two relations follow from the basic relations.)

For <math>\delta</math> a natural integer, let <math>V</math> be the natural representation of the general linear group <math>GL_\delta(\mathbb{C})</math>. 
The walled Brauer algebra <math>\mathfrak{B}_{r,s}(\delta)</math> has a natural action on <math> V^{\otimes r}\otimes (V^*)^{\otimes s}</math>, which is related by [[Schur-Weyl duality]] to the action of <math>GL_\delta(\mathbb{C})</math>.<ref name="cvdm07"/>
